contexts.text: He shall dwell in the tents of Shem () = that the internal things of worship may be in the external ones... The most ancients not only sojourned with tents, but also dwelt in tents... Hence to sojourn, and to dwell = to live.
The tent where He dwelt in man (); where the tent has a like signification to the temple, in which God is said to dwell, when He is present with man in love.

There have been shown me the dwellings of those who were of the second and third posterity of this Most Ancient Church; which are magnificent, extended to a great length, and variegated with beautiful colours, crimson and blue; for the Angels have most magnificent dwellings, beyond all description. I have seen them many times; they are so vividly apparent before their eyes, that nothing could possibly be more so.

And they dwelt there () = life thence. To dwell, in the Word, = to live. The term dwell occurs many times in both the prophetical and historical things of the Word, and for the most part = to live. The reason is, that the most ancients dwelt in tents... As tents = what is holy in worship, to dwell, in a good sense, = to live, or life. AC 1463:3.
On the dwellings of the Angels. General article.

All the Angels have their own dwellings, where they are, which are magnificent... The dwellings on earth are comparatively of no account; they call those on earth dead and not real, but their own living and true, because from the Lord...
The dwellings of good Spirits and of angelic Spirits. Described.
This is a sign that their dwellings are being changed into more pleasant ones.
As the Lord alone is righteousness, He is called the dwelling-place of justice ().
(Ishmael) shall dwell against the faces of all his brethren () = continual contentions in the things which are of faith, but that he will still be a victor.
They walk about... in their dwellings...
Under City, see this reference, and at AC 6015:4.

All the inhabitants of the cities () = that all goods were separated from them, so that there were nothing but evils in them. Inhabitants, when predicated of a city, = goods... Hence it is evident, that when a city = truth, an inhabitant = good; for truth is that in which good dwells; and the truth in which there is no good, is like an empty city, or one without an inhabitant. AC 2712.
(Lot) dwelt in the mountain () = that they betook themselves to a certain good.
Abraham dwelt between Kadesh and Shur () = the Lord's state in special. To dwell = to live.
Dwell in what is good in thine eyes () = that He was in everything where there was good... To dwell = to live; here, to be, because it is predicated of the Lord.
(Ishmael) dwelt in the wilderness () = what is relatively obscure. To dwell = to live.
He dwelt in the wilderness of Paran () = the life of the spiritual man as to good. To dwell is predicated of the good of truth, or of spiritual good, that is, of the good of the spiritual man.
That to dwell is predicated of good, or of the affection of truth. Illustrated.
Truths are inhabited by good.
No man () = no celestial good; no inhabitant = no spiritual good; no beast = no natural good.
To possess () is predicated of celestial good; to dwell, of spiritual good.
Man of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem () = those who are in the good of love, of charity and of faith.
The inhabitants of the gate () = evils and falsities; also the infernals.

Abraham dwelt in Beersheba () = that the Lord is this doctrine itself... To dwell in Beersheba = to be in doctrine, but, when predicated of the Lord, = doctrine itself; as to dwell in Heaven, which, too, is said of the Lord, not only = that He is in Heaven, but also that He is Heaven, for He is everything of Heaven.

The inhabitants of a city are in the Word sometimes called the men of the city; sometimes the inhabitants of the city: when they are called the men of the city, truths are signified; when the inhabitants, goods are signified.
In the Word it is frequently said... the man and the inhabitant; where man = that which is of the understanding, and inhabitant, that which is of the will. Illustrated.
No man () = no truth; no inhabitant = no good.
(Isaac) was dwelling in the laud of the south () = thence in Divine light. To dwell = to live, and is predicated of good. References.
Isaac dwelt with Beerlahairoi () = the Lord's Divine Rational in Divine light. To dwell = to live.

Isaac dwelt in Gerar () = the Lord's state as to those things which are of faith, relatively to the rational things which were to be adjoined. To dwell in Gerar = to be in those things which are of faith, thus state as to these things; for to dwell = to live.
That to dwell = to be and to live, thus state. Illustrated. AC 3417.
Babel shall not be inhabited to eternity () = their state of damnation.

In the whole inhabited [earth] () = the Christian world... The Church is here called inhabited from the life of faith, that is, from the good which is of truth; for to dwell = to live; and inhabitants = the goods of truth. References.
Behold, of the fatnesses of the earth is thy habitation () = life from Divine good... Habitation = life; and habitation is predicated of good. References.
To tarry is predicated of the life of truth with good; and to dwell, of the life of good with truth.
The inhabitant of Jerusalem = the good of the Church.
Of ignorance of both truth and good is predicated they found no city of habitation ().
(Jacob) dwelt with (Laban) a month of days () = a new state of life. To dwell = life.
What is affirmative... is as it were the first dwelling-place of the good flowing in from the Lord.
No cares for habitation, etc., there.

Hence Heaven is called the dwelling-place of God, as in Isaiah: Look forth from the Heavens, and see from the dwelling-place of Thy holiness and of Thy gracefulness... (). The dwelling-place of holiness = the Celestial Kingdom; and the dwellingplace of gracefulness, the Spiritual Kingdom; dwelling-place, here, is from the same word as that from which comes dwell together, and Zebulon. AC 8875:3. AC 9815:2.
To dwell in the passage of Jordan () = to be in those things which are initiaments.
Ye shall dwell with us () = life. To dwell = to live; thus to dwell with us = to live together, and to make one Church. AC 4452.
City = the truth of doctrine; and inhabitants, the good of doctrine; but when the inhabitants of a city are called the men of the city, not the good of doctrine, but its truths, are signified.
Let them dwell in the land () = as to life. To dwell = life... Thus to dwell in the land = a likeness of life according to those things which are of the Church. AC 4484. AC 4490.
The inhabitant of the land (), here, = those who were of the Ancient Church.
Not to dwell in the land of Jehovah () = not to be in the good of love.
To reside is predicated of truth; but to dwell, of good.
The dwellings of the blest in the other life are various, constructed with such art, that they are as it were in the very art of architecture, or immediately from that art.
Jacob dwelt in the land of the sojournings of his father... () = the Lord's Divine Natural living together with or concordant under Divine good rational. AC 4667.
To restore the paths to dwell () = the truths which are of good... To dwell is predicated of good.
Thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen () = the middle in the Natural. To dwell = to live.

In order that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen () = so shall your station be in the middle of the Natural where are the scientifics of the Church. To dwell = life, and thus the station of life. AC 6080. AC 6084.
And Joseph made his father and his brethren dwell () = the life of spiritual good and of the truths of the Church from the celestial internal. To dwell = life.
And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt () = that spiritual good lived among the scientifics which are of the Church. To dwell = to live.
He shall dwell at the haven of the seas () = life where there is the conclusion of truth from scientifics... To dwell = life.
The inhabitant of the Land, the Canaanite, saw the grievous mourning in the floor of Atad () = the apperception of grief by the good of the Church... Inhabitant = good.
Joseph dwelt in Egypt () = the life of the scientifics of the Church from the internal. To dwell = life.
To destroy the inhabitants in the city () = to destroy the goods which are derived from the doctrine of the Church.
Which end is a heavenly Kingdom, in which the Divine can dwell.
(Moses) dwelt in the land of Midian () = life among those who are in simple good.
And he dwelt near a well () = study there in the Word. To dwell = life; here, the study of life.
And Moses willed to dwell with the man () = that they agreed... To dwell = to live; and to dwell with anyone = to live together, and therefore to agree.
Conjunction through love and faith is signified by My dwelling shall be with them, etc. ().

And all the Sons of Israel had light in their habitations () = that with those who were of the Spiritual Church there was enlightenment in the mind everywhere... Habitations = the things which are of the mind; for a house = the mind of man; and bed-chambers, its interiors; but habitations, all things of the mind. To dwell, also, = to live; hence habitations = where are those things which are of life, that is, where are those things which are of intelligence and wisdom, which are the things of the mind. In the other life, too, in the habitations or abodes of the Angels, there is light according to the intelligence and wisdom of their minds.

In all your habitations ye shall eat unleavened things () = that in the interiors, where good is, truth shall be appropriated. Habitations = those things which are of the mind, thus which are of intelligence and wisdom; consequently, the interiors...

The habitation of the Sons of Israel which they dwelt in Egypt () = the duration of infestations. Habitation = states of life; here, states of infestations, for these are the states of life which are here treated of.

I will appoint for Him a dwelling () = that he will be in the good which is from Him as in His own Heaven. A dwelling, when said of the Lord, = good. The reason the dwelling of the Lord is good, is that all good is from the Lord... When the Lord dwells in this, He dwells in His own Divine, and cannot dwell anywhere else. Signified. It is said, as in His own Heaven, because Heaven is called the dwelling-place of God, from the fact that the good which is from the Lord is there, and constitutes Heaven.

Thou hast conducted them in Thy valour to the dwelling of Thy holiness () = that the Divine power of the Lord has elevated them to Heaven into the Divine there... The dwelling of holiness = Heaven where is the Divine.
That the dwelling of Jehovah or the Lord = Heaven; and also good, because in good there is Heaven. Illustrated.
That the dwelling of Jehovah, that is, of the Lord, is in good. Illustrated.
The inhabitants of Philistia () = those who are in faith alone.
The inhabitants of Canaan () = those who are of the Church, and who have adulterated goods and falsified truths.
A place for Thee to dwell () = where the Lord is... To dwell is predicated of good; and the dwelling of Jehovah = good, and thence Heaven.
The dwellings (of the inhabitants of Jupiter) have been shown me. Described.
The Angels with man as it were dwell in good from the Lord, and they cannot be in good from the man...

Until they came to an inhabited land () = before they came to Heaven, where there is good everywhere... Heaven is called an inhabited land, from good; for inhabited = what is living from good. References.
Under Angel, see this reference.
In (that which reigns universally with a man) dwell the Angels and Spirits who are with man, and have as it were their abode...
Charity and faith are Heaven... there, also, dwell the Angels.
Spirits and Angels have dwellings which appear just like those in the world (References.); and each and all things that appear in their dwellings, are significative of spiritual things...
The habitation of the Sons of Israel in Canaan...

The new will, where is the good of charity, is the dwelling of the Lord, and therefore Heaven with man; and the new Intellectual thence is as it were the tabernacle through which there is entrance and exit.
The Lord dwells with an Angel only in that which is His own with him; in like manner with a man... AC 10125. AC 10151:2. AC 10151:3, Explained.

I give into your hands the inhabitants of the Land () = command over evils... The inhabitants of the Land = the evils of the Church; for inhabitants = goods; and therefore in the opposite sense, evils. AC 9334:end.
They shall not dwell in thy Land () = that evils shall not be together with the goods of the Church. Inhabitants = evils... to dwell = to live; and to dwell with anyone = to live or be together.
Hence Heaven is called the dwelling-place of God... because a dwelling-place = the truth Divine proceeding from the Lord as received in the inmost Heaven, which, relatively, is good.
The dwelling-place of mount Zion () = Heaven and the Church.
The dwelling-place (or Tabernacle) = Heaven itself.

That I may dwell in the midst of them () = the consequent presence of the Lord in the representative Church. To dwell in the midst, when said of the Lord, = His presence; for to dwell = to be and to live. Hence to dwell in the midst = to be and to live present.

According to all that I show thee, the form of the dwelling-place () = a representative of Heaven where the Lord is. The form of the dwellingplace = a representative of Heaven; for form = a representative; and dwelling-place = Heaven.

As a dwelling-place = Heaven where the Lord is, it also = the good of love and of faith, for these make Heaven; and, as all good is from the Lord, and Heaven is called Heaven from love and faith in the Lord, in the supreme sense, a dwelling-place = the Lord. Illustrated.
Hence it is evident, that the Tabernacle was called the sanctuary and the dwelling-place of Jehovah from the fact that it represented the above-mentioned things.
We will enter into His dwelling-place ()... The dwelling-place = Heaven where the Lord is.
In like manner the dwelling-place of the sanctuary ().

By the whole Tabernacle or Tent was represented the universal angelic Heaven; its ultimate, by the court; its middle, by the dwelling-place where the priest ministered; and its inmost by the dwelling-place within the veil, where was the ark containing the Testimony.
The dwelling-place and court of the tent, and the curtains and veils there, represented the things which are in the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom, which is the Second Heaven. AC 9592.

Thou shalt make the dwelling-place () = the Second or middle Heaven. The dwellingplace, when said of what is Divine, = Heaven, properly the Second Heaven... The ark... represented the Third Heaven; the dwelling-place where was the table and the candlestick, the Second Heaven; and the court, the First Heaven.

Heaven is called the dwelling-place of God from the fact, that the Divine of the Lord dwells there; for it is the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord's Divine good which makes Heaven... And as the Lord dwells with the Angels in that which is from Himself, Heaven is called the dwelling-place of God; and the Divine truths themselves from the Divine good, of which the Angels or the angelic Societies are the receptions, are called dwelling-places. Illustrated.
That it is the Divine things which proceed from the Lord's Divine Human which are properly called dwelling-places, and that thence Heaven itself is called the dwelling-place. Illustrated.
Thus dwelling-place = Heaven, and also the Church where the Lord is.

How the Lord dwells in the Heavens, may be evident from (the fact) that the Lord as to the Divine Human is the Sun... in the Heavens; the heat from the Lord as a Sun is love, and the light is faith: the Lord thence dwells with those who receive from Him the good of love and the truth of faith... His presence is according to the degree of the reception.

From this it may be evident, that the Intellectual itself with those who are of the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom is the dwelling-place in a strict sense; and that this is described by the expanse from the curtains.

To stretch out the heavens and to expand the earth has a like signification to the stretching out and expanding of the dwelling-place by means of the curtains; and this signification is, to regenerate man, and thus create or form a new Intellectual in which there is a new Voluntary, which is the Heaven itself of the spiritual man, in which the Lord dwells with this man. AC 9596:6, Illustrated.
The dwelling-place shall be one () = that the whole Heaven is thus completely one. The dwelling-place = Heaven. AC 9776.
The whole conjunction of such innumerable angelic Societies in Heaven, with the methods thereof, is represented in the form of the construction of the dwelling-place and of the Tent...
Where it treats of the dwelling-place, by which is signified the internal of Heaven...

The half-curtain that is left over thou shalt make to overflow upon the hinder parts of the dwellingplace () = the ultimate of Heaven, to wit, the proceeding... The hinder parts of the dwelling-place = the ultimate of Heaven; for the dwelling-place = Heaven.

Thou shalt make boards for the dwellingplace () = the good supporting that Heaven... The dwelling-place = the Second Heaven... For the boards supported the curtains of both the dwelling-place and of the Tent, and also the two coverings over them. AC 9641. AC 9648. AC 9663.

Thou shalt place the dwelling-place according to the method which thou wast made to see in the mount () = to the quarters according to the states of good and thence of truth in the Heaven which is represented. The dwelling-place is a representative of Heaven.

It is evident from the description, that as to length the dwelling-place was set from east to west, and that the entrance was at the east, and the ark at the west; thus the sides were on the south and north. The eastern quarter of the dwelling-place represented the state of good at its rising; its western quarter, the state of good at its setting; its southern quarter, the state of truth at its rising; and its northern quarter, the state of truth in its shade. The entrance was at the eastern quarter, because the Lord enters into Heaven through the good of love. Illustrated.

The veil was that which distinguished between the dwelling-place where was the ark of the testimony, and where the candlestick and table were... By the dwelling-place outside the veil was represented the middle Heaven. AC 9684.

The court of the dwelling-place = the external of Heaven, thus the ultimate Heaven... The inmost Heaven is represented by the inmost of the dwellingplace where was the ark of the testimony; the middle Heaven, by the dwelling-place outside the veil; the ultimate Heaven, by the court.
The dwelling-place and the Tent = Heaven.

I will dwell in the midst of the Sons of Israel () = the presence of the Lord and His influx through good in Heaven and in the Church. To dwell, when said of the Lord, = to be present and to flow in. That it is through Divine good, is because to dwell is predicated of good. AC 10153:2, Explained. AC 10157.
The state of life of the golden age is described in the Word by to dwell under themselves securely and solitarily, without doors and bars. And as their dwellings were tents...

Take heed to thyself, lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitant of the land upon which thou comest () = that we are not to adhere to any religion whatever in which there is evil... The inhabitant of the land = religion in which there is evil; for an inhabitant = good; and therefore in the opposite sense, evil. AC 10647.
The Lord does not dwell with an empty man, that is, with a man who does not know His truths and do them...

Ye shall not kindle a fire in all your habitations on the Sabbath day () = that nothing of our Own love... ought to appear in each and all things of man which are from the Lord... The habitations of the Sons of Israel = the goods and truths of the Church which are with man from the Lord; for habitations = the interiors with man, thus those which are of his mind.
The dwellings (of the people of the Fifth Earth). Described.
From the parts of Heaven which are not inhabited...

Spirits and Angels dwell and dwell together cohabitant-in like manner as in the world... They who have dwelt congregated together in the world, dwell there congregated together; and they who have dwelt separate in houses and families, also dwell separate there in like manner. These Spirits (of the Sixth Earth) had dwelt separate in their own Earth... house by house, family by family, and thus nation by nation; and thus had not known what it was to dwell in society together.
Under Dominion, see this reference.
Hence it is, that in the Word, Heaven is called the dwelling-place of the Lord, and His throne.
From these things it is evident, that the Lord dwells in what is His own with the Angels. DLW 114. DP 53:end.
The Celestial Kingdom is also called... in the Word the Lord's dwelling-place.
There are also Angels who dwell solitary, as it were house by house, and family by family... HH 189. SE 5181.
All in the Heavens dwell distinct according to the quarters. Explained. HH 149.
They who are in the Hells also dwell according to their own quarters...
On the habitations and mansions of the Angels. General article.
The Angels have habitations, which are various according to each one's state of life, magnificent for those who are in greater dignity, and less so for those who are in lower rank.
As Angels are men, they have mansions and dwellings.
Everyone has a general idea that the Angels... have domiciles, which they call the dwelling-places of Heaven, and which are more magnificent than the dwelling-places of earth...

Whenever I have spoken with the Angels face to face, I have been with them in their dwellings. Their dwellings are just like the dwellings on earth, which are called houses, but more beautiful. In them, there are vaults, rooms, and bed-chambers in great numbers: there are also courts; and round about are gardens, shrubberies, and fields. Where the Angels are consociated, their dwellings are contiguous, one next another, disposed in the form of a city...
See Palace, and throughout.
Under House, see this reference. HH 190.

The Angels of the Celestial Kingdom dwell for the most part in lofty places... The Angels of the Spiritual Kingdom dwell in less lofty places... And the Angels in the lowest parts of Heaven, dwell in places which appear like ledges of stone.
These dwell in the midst of the Society, in a more elevated situation than the rest, and also in magnificent palaces.
The like Spirits are present, and as it were dwell in their affections.
He may dwell magnificently according to his condition. SE 5794.
When Angels are with men, they as it were dwell in their affections...
They dwell gratis. DLW 334, DLove 12:3.
It has been granted to see the extent of the inhabited Heaven, and also that of the not inhabited...
They who loved Divine truths and the Word from interior affection... in the other life dwell in light, in lofty places...
Habitations were then given them. LJ 51.
Where the habitations of the Papists have hitherto been in the Spiritual World...
My friend, come with me, and dwell with us.

As these quarters... are spiritual, the habitations of Angels and Spirits, all of which are according to these quarters, are also spiritual; and they are spiritual, because Angels and Spirits dwell according to their reception of love and wisdom from the Lord. (Explained.)
This diversity of their habitations appears as if it were from the Lord as a Sun, when yet it is from the Angels...

As the quarters are thus as it were inscribed on the Angel... he knows his own house and his own habitation wherever he goes. The reason a man does not know his house and habitation from the quarter in himself, is that he thinks from space... Nevertheless, birds and beasts... have it implanted in them to know of themselves their own homes and habitations.
Uses for the support of the body... habitation...
These uses may be described by (such terms as)... habitation... habitation being applied to Heaven.
That two receptacles and dwelling-places for Himself... have been created by the Lord with man...
Temporary things... relate to... habitation, etc.
The smaller part of the habitable world.
To know where thou dwellest () = to know of what quality it is; for, in the Spiritual World, everyone dwells according to the quality of his affection.
Angels dwell upon mountains...

He that sitteth upon the throne shall dwell over them () = that the Lord continually implants good in the truths which they receive from Him... (For), in the Word, to dwell is predicated of good. AE 479.
They that dwell upon the earth () = those who are in the Church where the Word is, and thereby the Lord is known.
They that dwell upon the earth () = those who are of the Church; here, those who are of this religiosity.
He shall dwell with them () = the conjunction of the Lord with them.

The reason to dwell with them = conjunction with them, is that to dwell = conjunction from love, as may be evident from many passages in the Word, and also from the habitations of the Angels in Heaven... For each Society is in one species of affection, and they dwell there distinctly according to the relationships and affinities of that species of affection... CL 50.
If anyone there loves another, he dwells with him in the same Society; and if he loves him inmostly, in the same house.
These most ancient people... dwelt in tabernacles; wherefore they now also dwell in them.
We perceive (these three regions of the mind) like stories in a house, one above another.
The mind of every man... actually dwells in one Society there...

If God were to do violence to the free will of man, the habitation of man in God would perish, and there would only be that of God in man; and this habitation is in all, both on earth and in the Heavens, and also in those who are in the Hells... But there is no reciprocal habitation of man in God, except with those who live according to the laws of order...
The human mind is distinguished into three regions, like a house into three stories, in like manner as the habitations of the Angels are into three Heavens.
Until He translates them into a certain better dwelling...
On the dwellings of those in the other life. SE 2477. Described. SE 4292, Described.
The dwellings of the most deceitful. Described.
That Spirits and Angels dwell in the affections of man.
1.2. They who are in a like affection dwell together, and this constantly.
The dwellings of the evil are there; for evil Spirits dwell in cavities and dark places, to which there is a descent by steps...
They know of what quality they are from their habitations in the city; for all there dwell according to their quality...
Where thou dwellest = among whom he now lives. To dwell = to live. Illustrated. AE 138. AE 215. AE 294:13. AE 365:13. AE 600:12. AE 601:7. AE 662:end. Illustrated. AE 721:13.
To dwell to eternity () = life and eternal salvation.
The dwelling-place that was outside the veil = the Second Heaven.
The inhabitant (of the city) = the good of doctrine.
The inhabitants of the earth = the goods of the Church.
I will fly away where I may dwell () = thereby to snatch the life from damnation.
The internal sense of the Word as to good is meant by the dwelling-place of Zion ().
The inhabitress of Zion () = the like as the daughter of Zion, namely, the Celestial Church, or the Church which is in the good of love to the Lord. AE 326:3.
The dwelling-place of the sanctuary () = the Church where these are.
The inhabitants of the rock () = the good of faith in them.
The inhabitants of the cities of Israel () = those who are in the affection of truth from good, that is, in the spiritual affection of truth, and thence in the doctrine of genuine truth.
His dwelling-place in Zion () = the good of love, since the Lord dwells in this...
The dwelling-place of peace () = Heaven where the Lord is.

There He maketh the hungry to dwell ()... To dwell = to live... That they may erect a city of habitation = that they may make for themselves the doctrine of life... Habitation = life. AE 730:25. AE 730:37.
Those Heavens are called dwelling-places where there is the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom, in which there reigns truth from this good.
How amiable are Thy dwelling-places ()... By dwelling-places are meant the higher Heavens.
They that dwell upon the earth () = those who are in the former Heaven which afterwards passed away; for they dwelt upon the earth, etc., in the Spiritual World.
The dwelling-places of the wilderness () = the interior things of the mind of those in whom they did not exist before.
Dwelling-places = where they are; here, therefore, the dwelling-places of the wilderness () = the falsities from the above-named evils.
The inhabitants of the islands () = the goods of truth of the natural man; for to dwell in the Word = to live; and inhabitants, the goods of life. AE 406:3. AE 406:5.
The faith of falsity is signified by a dwellingplace in a rock ().
These are meant by the inhabitress of the valley ()... Inhabitress = falsity of life.
In the Spiritual World, all dwell according to the correspondences of the interiors of their mind and life.
The habitations of Spirits and Angels succeed each other in this order... AE 422:7.
To dwell, in the Word, is said of goods.
(As they sit in the temples, so they dwell in the houses.)

Tabernacles and dwelling-places () = habitations such as there are in the Heavens; tabernacles, the habitations of those who are in the good of love; and dwelling-places, the habitations of those who are in truths from that good.

He that sitteth upon the throne shall dwell over them = the influx of Divine good into the truths with them... To dwell over them = to inflow with good into their truths; for to dwell, in the Word, is said of good; whence inhabitants = those who are in good...
The dwelling-place of mount Zion = the good of the Celestial Church. AE 594:15.
The inhabitants of the isle () = those who are in the goods of life according to their own doctrinal things.
They that dwell therein () = the universal Heaven as to its goods; inhabitants, in the Word, = those who are in the goods of Heaven and the Church, thus their goods. AE 518:38.
They that dwell upon the earth () = those who are of the Church.
As cities which are not inhabited () = as doctrines which are devoid of good. Not to dwell, here () = not to be in any truths because not in good; for these do not dwell in houses, but in pits.
To dwell in the house () = the appearance of spiritual life thence.
The dwelling-places of the shepherds () = all the goods of the Church.
To dwell before Jehovah () = to live from the Lord. AE 617:12. AE 1035.
To dwell with them to eternity () = the perpetual presence of the Lord with them. AE 630:11.
The dwelling-places of the wilderness () = those things which are of the understanding and will with such a man, which otherwise would receive the goods and truths of the Church.
Man-fir, and inhabitants, in the spiritual sense in the Word, = all who are in truths and in goods.
To make to dwell upon their own houses () = the interiors of the mind formed by means of truths from good, and thus safe from infestation by the falsities of evil.
The inhabitants of Jerusalem () = all things of the Church thence depending.
They that dwell upon] the earth () = those who are in the Church; here, those who are in evils and thence in falsities therein, thus who are against its goods and truths.
They that dwell upon the earth () = those who live in the Church; here, in the devastated Church.
His dwelling-places () = those things which are of the spiritual sense of the Word, and therefore the Heavens which are in that sense. 700 9.
The inhabitants (of Jericho) = the profane.
Heaven and the Church are called My sanctuary from the good of love; and My dwelling-place () from the truths of that good; for the Lord dwells in truths from good.
The inhabitants of the ends () = those who are in the ultimates of Heaven and the Church, and are there in the faith of charity.
No inhabitant () = no good with anyone.
The tents of Jacob, and his dwelling-places () = all things of the Church and of its doctrine; tents, its goods; and dwelling-places, its truths.
Dwelling-places () are said of the interiors of man, which are of his mind.
In the Spiritual World... the quality of everyone is known from the place where he dwells; and everyone knows the place where he dwells from his own quality.
To dwell = to live; and thence inhabitants = those who are in the good of doctrine and thence of life. References. AE 741:8.

Therefore rejoice ye Heavens, and ye that dwell in them () = the salvation and thence the joy of those who become spiritual through the reception of Divine truth... Ye that dwell = those who live; here, spiritually.
Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea () = lamentation over those who become merely natural and sensuous.

To make the desolate cities to be inhabited () = their life according to Divine truths, which had heretofore been destroyed; cities = the truths of doctrine from the Word; and to dwell = to live according to them.
The dwelling-place of Jehovah, and His tabernacle () = Heaven and the Church; dwelling-place, Heaven and the Church as to truths; and tabernacle, Heaven and the Church as to goods.
They that dwell upon the earth () = those who have been born within the Church; for the earth = the Church; and they that dwell upon it, = those who are and who live there...

The earth and they that dwell therein () = those who are of the Church in falsities and thence in evils... They that dwell on the earth = the goods or evils of the Church; here, the evils. AE 826. AE 827.
To evangelize to them that dwell upon the earth () = to announce the Lord's Advent to all who are of the Church.
The dwelling-place of demons () = where there are direful falsities from the truths and goods of the Church profaned...
The dwelling-places which are laid waste, so that there is not a man passing through them () = the doctrinal things of the Church, which were from the Word, in which there was not any good and truth.
1. [end]. The Lord does not dwell with man, except in his innocence.
